The priority LEVEL is questionable: the page says "Give urgent attention" and "refer urgently", which the house standard maps to Urgent; Emergency is reserved for explicit escalation (CPR, airway, BP < 90/60 with altered consciousness) or a warning sign that already carries that level. rule_level_problems.problem: The page's one explicit time threshold, "If fit has lasted >= 5 minutes ... refer urgently", is not encoded. No onset/time_ago comparison and no Status epilepticus diagnosis exist, so seizure duration never changes the output. This is the page's main escalation point.

Priority level Emergency is not justified by the page text. The red box says "Give urgent attention" and the algorithm says "refer urgently", which the house standard maps to Urgent (the gold standard's anaphylaxis red box is Urgent). Emergency is reserved for explicit escalation such as CPR or airway, or a warning sign that already carries that level; unconscious + fitting with ventilation on the page makes Emergency defensible, but it should be stated as a decision, and if the Seizure warning sign already carries a level this rule should agree with it.

Red-box glucose threshold not encoded: glucose < 3 mmol/L (< 4 if diabetic) in a fitting patient -> hypoglycaemia (page 19). Glucose is a routine vital with mmol/L available and "Hypoglycemia" (disorder) and "Diabetes mellitus" (disorder) exist, so a possible-Hypoglycemia rule was expressible; only "unable to measure" is not.

Red-box pregnancy criterion not encoded: fitting at >= 20 weeks pregnant or up to 1 week postpartum -> eclampsia (page 177). The 20-week threshold is not representable, but pregnancy / postpartum state as findings and "Eclamptic seizure" (finding) are, so a possible rule or at least check_for items were expected.

rule_level_problems.rule: Check for unconsciousness in the fitting patient
rule_level_problems.problem: The check_for list has a single item. The house standard says the list must include every item in the red box; current head injury, pregnancy/postpartum status, diabetes (for the 4 mmol/L threshold) and slow/shallow breathing are all red-box items that are expressible and absent. The one item present (Unconscious) is correctly consumed by the priority rule, and the task's due_to (Seizure) is the warning-sign concept, so the task itself is well-formed.

The rule requires both Seizure and Unconscious, which matches the header wording, but it means a patient recorded only as fitting (the Seizure warning sign) gets no priority from this page until the check_for has been answered. Acceptable if the Seizure warning sign already carries its own priority; flagged so a reviewer can confirm.

summary: The file encodes only the red-box header (unconscious + fitting -> priority) and misses every criterion inside the box: the >= 5 minute fit / refer-urgently threshold (the page's main escalation point, expressible with onset/time_ago), the glucose < 3 (< 4 if diabetic) hypoglycaemia threshold, and the >= 20 weeks pregnant / <= 1 week postpartum eclampsia routing. The one priority rule is logically correct but its Emergency level is not stated by the page, which says "urgent attention" and "refer urgently" and would map to Urgent under the house standard. The page has no "X likely" statements, so the absence of diagnosis rules is not itself a defect; the rest of the page is drug and airway management and is out of scope by design.
